title: Arjuna at the northern gate
hook: the four brothers ride to the four directions; at the edge of the world, Arjuna keeps a sacred limit
carry: maryada: some ground you don't take

segments.voice: Yesterday, on the road to the Rajasuya, a prison opened and Jarasandha's son was put on his father's throne. Your line was dharma-vijaya, win to set right, not to take.

Back at Indraprastha, the plan gets bigger. If kings are going to honor Yudhishthira, the brothers will have to go and meet them first. So the younger four divide the world. Arjuna rides north. Bhima rides east. Sahadeva rides south. Nakula rides west. Yudhishthira stays home in the hall, with Dhaumya and his friends around him. Each brother will come back with the tribute of kings. And one will come back from a place where there was nothing to win.
screen: `NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, WEST.` → `YUDHISHTHIRA STAYS HOME.` → `A PLACE WITH NOTHING TO WIN.`

segments.voice: The text follows each brother in turn: kingdoms, battles, and kings who submit or welcome them and send gifts. But one moment at the northern edge stands apart. Arjuna rides on, past mountain after mountain, to the land of the Northern Kurus. At the gate, powerful guards stop him, and they speak kindly. You can't conquer this place, they say. Even if you came in, you couldn't see anything with human eyes. We're pleased with you. Tell us what you want. And Arjuna doesn't push. I want my brother to be sovereign, he says. If this land is closed to humans, I won't enter. Give something as tribute, and I'll go. They give him fine cloth, ornaments and skins, and he turns back. The greatest archer of his age, who won Draupadi with his bow, meets a boundary and keeps it. Hindus have a word for that: maryada, the right limit, the line you don't cross even when you could. It's why Rama is called maryada purushottama, the best of men, who kept the bounds. And it's built into ordinary worship. Shoes come off at the temple door. Many people touch the step before they go in. And the inner shrine, the garbhagriha, where the murti sits, is in many temples for the priests alone; everyone else takes darshan from just outside. Holy ground is entered asking, not taking. This week ran from a father's message to a prison opened and four brothers coming home with the world's gifts. Tomorrow, the Rajasuya itself.
screen: `THE NORTHERN KURUS' GATE.` · `ARJUNA ASKS, AND TURNS BACK.` · `MARYADA: THE KEPT LIMIT.` · `SHOES OFF AT THE TEMPLE DOOR.` · then, large: `HOLY GROUND IS ENTERED ASKING.`

segments.voice: Find the nearest doorway, or picture the door of a temple or a place that's holy to you. Many Hindus touch the temple step, then their forehead, before they go in. If you pray, do that, or simply bow your head at the threshold and step through asking, not taking. If you don't, stop at the doorway for one slow breath and notice the line you're crossing.
The Rajasuya. Today the brothers ride to the four directions to win kings' tribute for it, and at the northern edge Arjuna keeps a limit.
Your line: maryada, some ground you don't take. The greatest archer stopped at a gate and asked. See you at the Rajasuya.

howItsDone: The word digvijaya, conquest of the directions, outlived the epic: tradition uses it for the travels of the teacher Shankara, whose victories are told as debates won across India rather than battles.

Northern Kurus.meaning: a land at the far north, closed to human eyes

maryada.meaning: the right limit, kept even when you could cross it

garbhagriha.meaning: a temple's inner shrine, where the murti sits

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Digvijaya Parva (the four brothers ride to the four directions; Arjuna at the land of the Northern Kurus)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm the assignment of directions: Arjuna north, Bhima east, Sahadeva south, Nakula west; Yudhishthira remaining at Indraprastha with Dhaumya and friends.
Confirm the Northern Kurus (Uttara Kurus) episode: kindly, powerful gatekeepers, 'nothing to conquer', 'nothing seen by human eyes', Arjuna's reply, and the tribute of cloth, ornaments and skins.
Arjuna winning Draupadi with his bow refers back to the swayamvara days.
Digvijaya glossed as 'victory over the directions' (dik + vijaya); this is a compound meaning, not a contested etymology, but confirm.
